key_findings: Epidermal Langerhans cell density increases in paw skin of male HFD mice in parallel with mechanical allodynia; in human PDN skin LC volume and dendritic complexity correlate with diabetes duration.
Genetic LC depletion (hLC-DTR + diphtheria toxin) prevents mechanical allodynia and spontaneous pain in male but not female HFD mice.
Male HFD LCs upregulate chemokine (CCL2, IL-18) and axon-guidance (Plxnb2, Plxna1) programs and are predicted to communicate with Mrgprd+ NP1 nociceptors via Sema4d/Sema6d and CCL2.
LCs release more CCL2 in HFD, and local intraplantar CCR2 antagonism reverses mechanical allodynia.
